title: service-messaging: a flow `notify` node can only address system users, so an applicant who came in through a public form never hears "received" or "rejected"
body:
Ruled: 6377887204 · batch #9 item 1 (#25496, 6377842908) · letter B · 2026-10-24T00:43:45Z (recipient = a record field of type email only; templated; rate-limited per address; logged)

Filed from the objectstack-ai/hotsrm v0.1 platform evaluation, 2026-10-23, spec 18.0.0.

## What was measured
- A public form (ADR-0138 guest model) creates a supplier application; the record flow fires, de-duplicates, blocks blacklisted companies and notifies the category manager in-app. All of that works.
- The `notify` node's recipients must be users. The applicant is not a user yet (they only become one if admitted), so the application's own outcome ("received", "returned for documents", "rejected") cannot reach them. No related issue was found.
- The only alternative is an `http` node to an external mail service, which needs credentials that the open tier keeps as environment variables, outside the package.

## Wanted
- A `notify` (or `email`) node recipient form that is an address taken from a record field (`record.contact_email`), rendered through the same template mechanism, subject to the environment's outbound mail configuration.
- Rate limiting and the usual guest-input sanitising apply since the address was typed by an anonymous visitor.

## Acceptance
A record flow on a public-form object sends a templated email to the address in one of the record's email fields, with no user account involved, and the send is visible in the messaging log.

Dedupe words: notify node email recipient non-user record field address public form applicant notification.
